subject.title: Improve context overflow error message with specifics

question: Which context-overflow facts should OpenClaw show to end users, and what redaction policy should apply to session/channel identifiers?
rationale: The code already has token, model, route, and session facts, but exposing raw session keys/channel identifiers and exact counts changes user-facing privacy and support behavior, so automation should not choose the policy alone.

options.title: Show redacted diagnostics
options.body: Expose provider/model, effective context budget, estimated or observed token count, overage, and a redacted channel/session label while keeping raw identifiers in logs.

options.title: Keep specifics operator-only
options.body: Leave chat copy generic and document logs/status metadata as the place to inspect detailed context-pressure facts.

options.title: Defer to broader visibility design
options.body: Keep this issue open until a broader context-visibility design decides channel messages, UI, logs, and status surfaces together.

recommendation.title: Show redacted diagnostics
recommendation.body: Expose provider/model, effective context budget, estimated or observed token count, overage, and a redacted channel/session label while keeping raw identifiers in logs.
